concepts.title: From Self to Family: The Widening Lens
concepts.definition: Unit II turns the discipline's lens outward: having understood the adolescent self, it now studies the family -- the first and most enduring institution -- and the community and society in which families are embedded and by which they are shaped.
concepts.key_idea: The self is the starting point; family, community and society are the widening circles it lives within.
concepts.textbook_ref: kehe107.txt unit opener (unit ii understanding family community and society, from self to family, institutions that shape decision making)
question_patterns: why does the course move from self to family and society
in class 11 understanding family community and society: what does this unit study

name the chapters covered under this unit

solution_steps.explain: Unit I studied the self -- identity, food, resources, media -- factors of personal decision making.
The family adds roles, relationships and shared resources that reshape individual choices.
Community institutions and larger social norms frame what families can and do decide.

concepts.title: The Family as the Basic Institution
concepts.definition: The family is humanity's basic social institution: it bears and rears children, transmits culture and values, and provides economic and emotional support. Its forms vary -- nuclear, joint, extended, single-parent -- but its functions of care, socialisation and support remain central to every society.
concepts.key_idea: First school, first economy, first refuge -- the family performs society's most intimate functions.
concepts.textbook_ref: kehe107.txt unit opener and family sections (family as basic institution, functions of family, types of family, care and support)
question_patterns: why is the family called the basic unit of society
in class 11 understanding family community and society: what functions does a family perform
how do families transmit culture to children
what support does a family provide its members
how have family forms changed in modern times

solution_steps.explain: Reproduction and rearing, socialisation into values, economic cooperation, and emotional care define the family's work.
Nuclear, joint, extended and single-parent households all can perform these functions differently.
Whatever the form, the family links the individual to society's larger patterns.

concepts.title: Community and Society as Frameworks of Family Life
concepts.definition: Families never live alone: neighbourhoods, schools, workplaces and services form the community, and larger social structures -- laws, economy, culture -- form society. Understanding family life therefore means reading these frameworks, from community resources to social expectations, that support or strain the household.
concepts.key_idea: Behind every family stand its community's services and society's rules -- read them to read the family.
concepts.textbook_ref: kehe107.txt unit opener sections (community and society context, institutions influencing families, resources of the community)
question_patterns: how does the community support family life
in class 11 understanding family community and society: distinguish community from society
what social institutions influence the family

how do social expectations shape family decisions

solution_steps.explain: Schools, clinics, markets and neighbourhood networks supply the family's daily supports.
Laws, economy and cultural norms set the wider terms within which families function.
Family decisions -- schooling, work, marriage -- are negotiated between these two frameworks.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Explain why a book for adolescents turns, in Unit II, from the self to the family and society.

solution_template.explain: Unit I built self-understanding -- identity, health, resources, media.

solution_template.action: state the need for the second
solution_template.explain: No self grows outside relationships; family, community and society are where the self acts.
The widening lens mirrors development itself -- from personal to social understanding.

worked_examples.question_pattern: A joint family decides together where a cousin will study, while a nuclear family decides alone. Relate both cases to the family's functions.

solution_template.explain: Both families perform the same function -- supporting a member's education and future.
The joint family pools opinions and resources; the nuclear family concentrates the decision in parents.
Forms vary, functions persist -- the chapter's view of the family as a basic institution.
